acceptance_criteria.criterion: WorkflowState includes prev_wp_summaries: list and run_start_ts: str
run_start log entry contains run_start_ts ISO timestamp
run_start_ts is passed to the graph initial state
run_end log entry contains total_duration_s (float, wallclock seconds)
Graceful handling when run_start_ts is missing (duration omitted, no crash)

summary: Added prev_wp_summaries: list and run_start_ts: str fields to WorkflowState in orchestrator/src/state.py under a new '--- Progress tracking ---' section.

Updated orchestrator/src/cli.py: extended module-level import to include datetime class; captured run_start_ts = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() before the run_start log entry; added run_start_ts to the run_start log call; added prev_wp_summaries and run_start_ts to the graph initial_state dict; computed total_duration_s in run_end with graceful fallback (try/except omits the field if run_start_ts is missing or unparseable).
Updated orchestrator/tests/test_state.py: added PROGRESS_TRACKING_FIELDS = {'prev_wp_summaries', 'run_start_ts'} set and included it in _all_expected() so test_no_unexpected_fields continues to pass.

All 111 synchronous unit tests pass (43 state+CLI, 68 config/plan/filelock). Pre-existing async test failures (154) are unrelated environment issues (pytest-asyncio not configured) and unchanged by this WP.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/cli.py: _make_dryrun_node() has a local 'from datetime import datetime' import that is now redundant since datetime is imported at module level. Safe to remove as a follow-up cleanup.

orchestrator/src/cli.py: run_end uses a dict-unpacking pattern (run_end_kwargs) instead of the inline run_logger.log() style used everywhere else in the file. Acceptable for conditional fields, but the pattern diverges slightly from local convention.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection and test execution.
AC1: WorkflowState.prev_wp_summaries (list) and run_start_ts (str) confirmed present in orchestrator/src/state.py under '--- Progress tracking ---' section.
AC2: run_start log entry confirmed to include run_start_ts=run_start_ts in cli.py run_logger.log() call.
AC3: run_start_ts confirmed present in initial_state dict passed to graph.ainvoke().
AC4: total_duration_s computed as round(...total_seconds(), 1) — float — and conditionally written to run_end log entry.
AC5: try/except (ValueError, TypeError) guards duration computation; total_duration_s omitted from run_end_kwargs when None — no crash path possible.

AC6: 111 synchronous unit tests pass (43 state+cli, 68 config/plan/filelock). test_state.py was updated to register new fields in PROGRESS_TRACKING_FIELDS — a necessary and correct adjustment; the 148 async failures are pre-existing pytest-asyncio environment issues unchanged by this WP.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/cli.py: _make_dryrun_node() has a local 'from datetime import datetime' that is now redundant — datetime is already imported at module level (line 28). Safe to remove as a follow-up cleanup.

orchestrator/src/cli.py: run_end uses a dict-unpacking pattern (run_end_kwargs) for conditional total_duration_s, diverging slightly from the inline run_logger.log() style used everywhere else. Acceptable for conditional fields; not a blocking issue.

orchestrator/tests/test_state.py: AC6 says 'Existing tests pass without modification' but test_state.py was modified to add PROGRESS_TRACKING_FIELDS. The change was necessary and correct (test_no_unexpected_fields would fail otherwise), and the modification is minimal and appropriate. AC6 spirit is fully met; the wording was implicitly contradictory for tests that enumerate state fields.

summary: Reviewed three modified files: orchestrator/src/state.py, orchestrator/src/cli.py, orchestrator/tests/test_state.py.
state.py: Two new fields under a well-named '--- Progress tracking ---' section. Bare list/str types are consistent with the rest of WorkflowState. Inline WP-ID comments improve traceability.

cli.py: run_start_ts capture uses datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() — timezone-aware, correct round-trip via fromisoformat(). run_start_ts flows correctly into both the run_start log entry (AC2) and initial_state (AC3). Duration computation is properly guarded by try/except (ValueError, TypeError) (AC5). run_end_kwargs dict-unpacking is the appropriate pattern for conditional field injection.

test_state.py: PROGRESS_TRACKING_FIELDS = {'prev_wp_summaries', 'run_start_ts'} addition follows existing naming conventions and is correctly included in _all_expected(). The test modification is necessary and correct.
Security: no issues — timestamps generated server-side, no user input, no injection surface.
Performance: trivial overhead (one datetime.now call), no additional MCP calls.
All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/cli.py: _make_dryrun_node() retains a local 'from datetime import datetime' import (line ~218) that is now redundant — datetime is imported at module level (line 28). Harmless but stale. Remove in a follow-up pass.

orchestrator/src/cli.py: run_end uses the run_end_kwargs dict-unpacking pattern for conditional total_duration_s, which diverges from the inline run_logger.log() style used elsewhere. This is the correct approach for conditional fields and is not a blocking issue; simply worth noting for any future style guide.

orchestrator/src/state.py: Inline WP-ID comments on new fields (e.g. '# … (WP-001)') are helpful for traceability but will become stale if plan archives are removed. Consider documenting this annotation convention in the project manifest constraints so future developers follow the same pattern consistently.
